title: Revealed Preference Analysis of Shapley-Scarf Housing Markets
abstract: arXiv:2512.23352v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We ask what the reallocation of indivisible objects reveals about the market that produced it. A central authority assigns the objects, after which recipients exchange them among themselves. Preferences are never observed, and individuals of the same type have identical preferences. A reallocation is rationalizable as Pareto efficient and individually rational exactly when a directed graph built from the data is acyclic, and as weak core-stable exactly when a mixed graph admits an orientation acyclic within types and free of alternating cycles. Deciding the latter is NP-complete, and on the single-crossing domain, although the test becomes more restrictive, it turns out to be more useful in practice. Both properties are less demanding than the strict core, so their rejection eliminates a broader set of possibilities. We apply the tests to administrative data on social housing lettings in England.

translated_title: Shapley-Scarf住房市场的显示性偏好分析
translated_abstract: arXiv:2512.23352v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：我们探讨不可分割物品的再分配揭示了产生该分配的市场信息。一个中央机构分配物品，之后接收者之间相互交换。偏好从未被观察，同一类型的个体具有相同偏好。当且仅当从数据构建的有向图无环时，一种再分配可被合理化理解为帕累托有效且个体理性；当且仅当混合图在类型内允许无环定向且无交替循环时，可被合理化理解为弱核稳定。判定后者是NP完全的，在单交叉域上，虽然测试变得更加严格，但在实践中更有用。这两个性质比严格核要求更低，因此其拒绝排除了更广泛的可能性。我们将这些测试应用于英格兰社会住房出租的行政数据。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于显示性偏好的方法，通过构建图结构来检验不可分割物品再分配是否可合理化，并应用于英格兰社会住房数据，发现弱核稳定性测试虽计算复杂但在单交叉域中更实用。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a revealed preference approach to test whether reallocations of indivisible objects are rationalizable, applying it to English social housing data, finding that weak core stability tests, though NP-complete, are more practical on single-crossing domains.
